subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- November 20, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - November 20, 2026

Good morning from Spokane! The team has been busy this week refining the privacy controls that make AcreetionOS stand out. Natalie pushed significant updates to our consent infrastructure, implementing a proper default-denied Consent Mode v2 snippet that loads before Google Tag Manager. The analytics page now features honest disclosure text about GTM-WW9RFH5B with GA4 completely removed, reflecting our commitment to transparency over tracking.

On the desktop side, Darren resolved a pesky bottom-bar icon clickability issue in the XLibre branch while also updating Electron to its latest version for new users. These fixes improve the first-run experience and ensure our Cinnamon-based environment feels polished from the moment you log in. The AcreetionOS-Xlibre repository continues to mature as our custom display server foundation.

We also launched the acreetionos-wallpapers repository with an initial commit and submodule tracking tied to our GitLab instance. This gives us a dedicated home for the emerging wallpaper collection that showcases our signature emerald-black and neon-purple aesthetic. Separately, the blog deployment pipeline now correctly sets the SITE variable for GitHub Pages, so blog.acreetionos.org builds cleanly with each push.

In broader community news, LLVM's relicensing effort is wrapping up after extensive discussion across the compiler ecosystem. This milestone matters for downstream distributions like ours that rely on LLVM toolchains for building and system libraries. The resolution brings clarity to licensing terms that affect everything from compiler runtime to GPU compute stacks.

Vim Classic 8.3.1 arrived this week, continuing the maintenance-focused fork that prioritizes stability over feature churn. For users who prefer a predictable editing experience without the rapid changes in upstream Vim, this release offers bug fixes and compatibility improvements. Our default installation includes Vim Classic as the system vi, and we track these releases closely for ISO refreshes.
